edbDesc: A gravitational lens is formed when the light from a very distant, bright source (such as a quasar) is 'bent' around a massive object (such as a cluster of galaxies) between the source object and the observer. The process is known as gravitational lensing, and is one of the predictions of Albert Einstein's general theory of relativity.
title: Gravitational Lensing
pickWhy: Bending of light by gravity is one of the predictions on the deck's general-relativity card; lensing itself needs galaxy-scale masses.
